abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) is a major global crop characterized by high genetic and phenotypic diversity across accessions. To better understand this diversity, the Genomes-to-Fields initiative has produced paired genotypic and phenotypic datasets annually since 2014. Here, we present 15 genome assemblies representing 13 maize lines, including founders and testers from the 2022-2023, 2024-2025, and 2026-2027 Genomes-to-Fields evaluation cycles and additional breeding germplasm, together with gene and repeat annotations. Assemblies ranged from 2.19 to 2.38 Gb, with BUSCO completeness of 97.9-99.0%. Excluding the more fragmented LH287 assembly (contig N50 = 5.3 Mb; 90.8% chromosome placement), contig N50 values ranged from 31.1 to 195.8 Mb, with 95.9-99.4% of sequence placed on chromosomes. Gene annotation identified approximately 40,000 gene models per genotype, of which 93.6-93.9% were classified as protein-coding, with 95.9-97.3% complete BUSCOs. Comparison with B73 identified 27,606-30,517 one-to-one syntenic orthologs per genotype, representing 69.4-76.8% of B73 genes. Transposable elements occupied 83.6-88.6% of the genomes, with LTR retrotransposons representing the predominant class. Comparative genome alignments revealed three large inversions, including a 12.65-Mb inversion on chromosome 3 present in six of the 13 lines. Together, these resources expand the genomic representation of maize breeding germplasm and provide a foundation for investigating genetic variation underlying agronomic traits.
